pre_condition: self.state_units is initialized and usable for capture.
The caller has established every quiescence condition required by participating state-unit contracts; this body performs no explicit stop, freeze, lock, generation check, or transactional boundary.

No mutation may change the participating unit identity domain or snapshot-owned logical values across the capture interval unless StateUnits::save and StateUnits::inventory jointly guarantee a stable-generation view.
Optional or intentionally unsaved units have a defined omission/default semantics compatible with the intended restore operation.
post_condition: On success, the function returns SavedState { units, inventory }, where units is exactly the concrete value returned by the completed self.state_units.save().await call and inventory is obtained from self.state_units.inventory() after that save call completes.

Subject to the StateUnits contracts and the quiescence precondition, units denotes the snapshot-owned logical projection of all participating units, while inventory identifies the compatible unit identity domain for that projection.

The result does not represent equality with the entire LoadedVm or destination runtime. Prepared memory, host resource bindings, worker channels, and other runtime-owned state are excluded unless a participating state-unit contract explicitly projects them into saved logical state.
Concrete serialization format, blob identity, and collection order are not semantically observable except where a state-unit or compatibility contract explicitly makes them observable.
Completeness, coherence, and same-generation correspondence between units and inventory are conditional properties; this body does not establish them independently.
failure_condition: The function returns the error produced by self.state_units.save().await and does not construct or return a SavedState.
Because inventory() is evaluated only after save succeeds, this body does not observe or return inventory on the error path.
The body provides no rollback or atomicity guarantee. StateUnits::save may have inspected, serialized, or otherwise processed a proper subset of units before failing.
No partial capture is exposed through this return value, but any internal side effects or retained partial work are governed solely by the StateUnits::save contract.

abstract_state.observable_state: A pair (I, V), where I is the inventory/identity domain of participating state units and V maps each intentionally captured identity in I to its snapshot-owned logical component state.
abstract_state.identity_domain: I records unit identities, kinds, versions, dependencies, or other compatibility metadata required to interpret and restore V.
abstract_state.captured_values: V contains logical state values, not serialization-buffer identity, incidental blob layout, iteration order, or runtime object identity.
abstract_state.excluded_state: Destination-owned and host-owned runtime state, including prepared memory, host bindings, worker channels, and other reconstruction infrastructure, unless explicitly owned by a state-unit snapshot contract.
abstract_state.completion_status: Success denotes a complete pair only if StateUnits::save guarantees all required units were captured and inventory denotes that same unit generation; failure denotes no caller-visible snapshot value, not necessarily no work.

abstraction.projection: Project LoadedVm through its participating state units: P(vm) = (Inventory(U, g), {id -> LogicalSnapshot(unit_id, g) | id is required or intentionally present}), for one stable generation g. SavedState is a representation of P(vm), not of vm in full.
abstraction.preserved_state: State outside P(vm) is not asserted equal across save and restore. A later round-trip theorem should require equality only of the snapshot-owned logical projection and should separately require reconstruction or preservation of destination-owned and host-owned state.
hidden_representation: Temporary buffers and partial intermediate results
Locks, worker channels, host handles, prepared memory, and destination bindings
Any omitted optional-unit representation whose semantics are defined as absence or default
abstraction.observation_boundary: The concrete body first awaits StateUnits::save to completion and then calls StateUnits::inventory. Therefore its literal observation interval begins when save starts and ends when inventory returns. A single quiescent capture boundary exists only if external quiescence spans this whole interval or the two StateUnits operations share an internal stable generation. The body itself introduces no atomic boundary.

obligations.title: Same-generation capture
obligations.claim: There exists one generation g such that every saved logical unit value and the returned inventory are observations of the participating state-unit set at g.
obligations.why_blocking: Without this property, inventory may describe a different compatible-unit domain than the saved values, preventing a coherent snapshot interpretation and a restore round-trip theorem.

suggested_callees.reason: Determine whether capture pins membership, records a generation, or otherwise guarantees a stable identity domain.
Determine whether inventory is immutable, generation-tagged, or derived from the exact set used by save.

obligations.title: Quiescent logical values
obligations.claim: All snapshot-owned logical values are observed at one valid quiescent boundary, or concurrent evolution is linearized to an equivalent single boundary.
obligations.why_blocking: Per-unit values captured at incompatible times can form a state that never existed and may violate cross-unit invariants after restore.

suggested_callees.reason: Establish whether save linearizes capture or assumes units have already been stopped.

obligations.title: Required-unit completeness
obligations.claim: On success, every required participating identity in the applicable inventory has exactly one semantically valid captured value, except identities whose contracts intentionally define omission.
obligations.why_blocking: A successful but partial unit map cannot support a complete projection restore unless missing values have explicit semantics.

suggested_callees.reason: Specify iteration, required-unit handling, duplicate detection, and success criteria.

obligations.title: Optional and unsaved semantics
obligations.claim: For every optional, skipped, stateless, or unsaved unit, inventory and restore define whether absence means default initialization, destination preservation, incompatibility, or intentional non-participation.
obligations.why_blocking: The round-trip projection cannot distinguish intended omission from lost state without a total interpretation of absence.

suggested_callees.reason: Identify how optional or non-saving units are represented in captured state.
Identify whether omitted units remain in the identity domain and how their capability is recorded.

obligations.title: Failure and partial-work semantics
obligations.claim: If any unit capture fails, no SavedState is returned; any already-performed work cannot be mistaken for a committed snapshot, and internal side effects satisfy a documented retry or cleanup policy.
obligations.why_blocking: The body prevents a returned partial value but does not ensure safe retry, rollback, or absence of unit-visible side effects.

suggested_callees.reason: Characterize ordering, side effects, retained buffers, cleanup, and retry behavior after a mid-capture error.

obligations.title: Representation independence
obligations.claim: Two SavedState values that encode the same inventory domain and logical per-unit values are observationally equivalent despite serialization bytes, map order, or traversal order, except for explicitly versioned representation constraints.
obligations.why_blocking: A projection round-trip theorem should compare logical state rather than incidental encoding details.

suggested_callees.reason: Connect concrete saved blobs to logical unit-state values.

obligations.title: Snapshot ownership boundary
obligations.claim: Each captured field is classified as snapshot-owned logical state, while destination-owned or host-owned runtime resources are excluded or represented only through portable logical descriptors.
obligations.why_blocking: Restore equivalence must not demand equality of host handles, channels, prepared memory, or other runtime artifacts, and must not accidentally serialize nonportable bindings.

suggested_callees.reason: Establish the ownership and portability of each unit's projected state.

obligations.title: Restore projection round-trip
obligations.claim: For compatible inventory I and logical projection V, restoring a concrete SavedState representation of (I, V) into a valid destination and then projecting the restored VM yields (I, V), modulo documented optional/default equivalences.
obligations.why_blocking: This is the desired composition theorem; save alone only supplies one side of the relation.

candidate_variants.name: Strong atomic snapshot
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Success represents all required participating units and inventory from one internally linearized generation, without requiring external quiescence beyond invoking save in an allowed lifecycle state.
candidate_variants.discriminator: StateUnits::save and inventory expose or prove a shared generation/lock transaction, and a mutation injected concurrently with capture is either excluded or wholly ordered before or after the returned snapshot.

candidate_variants.name: Caller-quiesced coherent snapshot

candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Success means only that one StateUnits::save call completed and its opaque result was paired with inventory observed afterward; completeness, cross-unit coherence, and same-generation identity are not promised.

obligations.claim: Each captured field is snapshot-owned logical state, while destination-owned and host-owned resources are excluded or represented only through portable logical descriptors.
obligations.why_blocking: Restore equivalence must neither require equality of runtime handles and channels nor accidentally preserve nonportable host bindings.

suggested_callees.reason: Establish ownership and portability of every unit's projected state.

obligations.title: Restore projection round-trip
obligations.claim: For compatible inventory I and logical projection V, restoring a representation of (I, V) into a valid destination and then projecting the restored VM yields (I, V), modulo documented optional and default equivalences.
obligations.why_blocking: This is the desired composition theorem; the shown save body provides only the capture-side packaging step.

candidate_variants.name: Strong atomic snapshot
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Success represents every required participating unit and inventory from one internally linearized generation, without requiring external quiescence beyond an allowed lifecycle state.
candidate_variants.discriminator: StateUnits exposes or proves a shared generation or lock transaction, and concurrent mutation is either excluded or wholly ordered before or after the returned snapshot.

candidate_variants.name: Caller-quiesced coherent snapshot
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Success is coherent and complete only when the caller freezes both unit membership and snapshot-owned values for the entire interval from save invocation through inventory observation.
candidate_variants.discriminator: No internal atomic generation is available, but lifecycle or synchronization evidence proves mutation is impossible across the full function call.

candidate_variants.name: Weak packaging contract
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Success means only that one StateUnits::save call completed and its opaque result was paired with inventory observed afterward; completeness, coherence, and same-generation identity are not promised.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Neither a shared internal generation guarantee nor a caller-enforced quiescence protocol can be established.

uncertainties: Whether StateUnits::save captures units sequentially, concurrently, or from a previously frozen view.
Whether StateUnits::inventory is immutable for the lifetime of LoadedVm or can change through registration, removal, replacement, or interior concurrency.
Whether save and inventory carry an implicit or explicit shared generation identifier.
Whether caller lifecycle rules guarantee that workers and devices are stopped before LoadedVm::save is invoked.
Whether cross-unit invariants require a globally simultaneous observation rather than individually consistent unit snapshots.
Which units are required, optional, stateless, destination-owned, or intentionally unsaved.
Whether a successful StateUnits::save may omit failed or unsupported units while still returning success.
Whether StateUnits::save has side effects and whether a failed capture can be retried safely.
Whether inventory contains sufficient compatibility metadata to interpret every saved unit value.
Whether restore treats collection order or concrete serialization representation as observable.
Whether host resources are represented by portable logical descriptors or embedded as runtime-specific state.
parsed_json.recommended_next_step: Expand O1 first using only the contracts of StateUnits::save and StateUnits::inventory. Determine whether they establish a shared stable generation. If they do not, evaluate O2 against the caller lifecycle protocol; if neither internal atomicity nor full-interval caller quiescence is established, retain the weak packaging contract and test concurrent membership mutation as a challenged bug hypothesis.
